newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday officially brought up the issue of a 'social Maastricht' during his visit to Sweden, saying the problems of "employment, growth, inequalities can only be dealt with by a joint supra-national policy".

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos yesterday reiterated Athens' desire to normalise relations with Turkey by signing "a non-conditional non-aggression pact", despite mass incursions of Greek airspace by Turkish fighter planes yesterday and Ankara's insistence on dialogue on the gamut of issues.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy will submit a bill in Parliament today that seeks to bolster the office of president of the republic to a watchdog of the constitutionality of government laws.

--The issue of who controls the archives of late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou has set the fur flying once again in ruling party PASOK, with Papandreou's widow Dimitra outlining to the party that it was her late husband's wish that she run the foundation in his name.
--Athens sees the sixth day of the rubbish collectors strike today, with mountains of festering garbage on every street corner.

--A Thessaloniki lawyer was arrested yesterday on suspicion of organising a baby-adoption racket with Greek, German, American and Swedish couples adopting infants from Russia, Albania, Bulgaria and Romania.
--A new agriculture ministry bill on forest land has drawn opposition from within the government and from the opposition.
--ND leader Costas Karamanlis yesterday made an impressive European debut at Brussels.
--Thousands are expected to resort to the courts to receive backpay for family benefits following the Supreme Court's decision that both parents could receive it.
